companies.name: BrainCo
companies.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

It also serves government agencies with licensing, subsidy management, enrollment coordination, and statewide substitute-teacher pools, and offers employers child care benefit programs. Backed by a16z and Uncork Capital, Wonderschool operates as a B2B/B2G SaaS business; it publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center (SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF) but no public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks were found during enrichment.

companies.name: Educative
companies.description: Educative is an online learning platform that provides high-quality, interactive courses for developers of all skill levels. With a focus on practical, hands-on learning, Educative offers courses on a wide range of topics, from programming languages like Python and JavaScript to data structures and algorithms. Each course is created by expert instructors and includes quizzes, coding challenges, and real-world projects to help learners apply their knowledge.

companies.name: Hiphen Plant
companies.description: Hiphen Plant provides advanced image analytics solutions for agricultural research. As plant scientists, they build tools that revolutionize how plants can be assessed, bringing the power of image analytics to agricultural research programs for decision-making on genetics, chemistry, and practices.

companies.name: Brisk Teaching
companies.description: Brisk Teaching is a K-12 education technology company that integrates AI directly into the tools teachers already use. Its platform spans three connected products: the Brisk Extension (which brings AI into Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, and YouTube), Brisk Boost (a safe, teacher-controlled, student-facing AI workspace), and Brisk Next (a web-based planning and instruction hub). Brisk helps educators give feedback, create instructional materials, change reading levels, inspect student writing, and generate presentations, lesson plans, rubrics, quizzes, IEP goals, and math problems. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Brisk publishes an llms.txt for AI representation and a public status page, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks its public surface.

companies.name: IKI AI

companies.name: On Deck
companies.description: On Deck (now operating as the On Deck Founder Fellowship, ODF) is a founder fellowship and startup community program that helps aspiring entrepreneurs start companies through an intense, in-person cohort experience focused on meeting co-founders, exploring ideas, and gaining conviction. Backed by Canaan Partners, On Deck provides mentorship, a peer community, and startup perks. It is a program and community platform rather than a developer or API product: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

companies.name: Quizlet
companies.description: Quizlet is a San Francisco-based global learning platform offering flashcards, practice tests, and AI-powered study tools used by students, teachers, and lifelong learners. Core features include user-created and expert-verified study sets, Learn mode (adaptive practice), Test mode, Match game, Spaced Repetition, and an AI tutor (Q-Chat / Magic Notes) that generates flashcards, summaries, practice questions, and explanations from uploaded notes, PDFs, slides, and textbooks. Quizlet Plus is the company's consumer subscription, and Quizlet for Schools / Teachers provides licensed offerings for classrooms. The platform integrates with Google Classroom (share-as-assignment) and Canvas (embeddable widgets) but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK — the legacy Developer API 2.0 (`quizlet.com/api/2.0`) was effectively wound down to partners-only and is not openly registrable. Quizlet's GitHub organization (`github.com/quizlet`) hosts internal tooling, GitHub Actions, and forks of OSS dependencies (HHVM/Hack, PHPUnit, Mockery, Stylus, etc.) rather than a developer-facing API platform.

companies.name: Sidechat
companies.description: Sidechat is an anonymous, campus-based social networking app for college students, built by Flower Ave Inc in New York City and backed by Canaan Partners. Students verify with a school email to join their college's private, location- and campus-scoped community where they post text, images, and polls, vote, and chat anonymously in a Reddit-like feed. Sidechat launched in early 2022, acquired Yik Yak in 2023, and operates primarily as an iOS consumer app. It publishes no official public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; this profile captures the company's public web presence and identity for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Brilliant
companies.description: Brilliant is a consumer-first interactive STEM learning platform that delivers bite-sized, problem-solving-driven courses in math, computer science, data science, and science to over 10 million learners on web, iOS, and Android. Brilliant for Educators offers free Premium access to K-12 teachers and students, with Google Classroom roster sync, COPPA/FERPA/GDPR compliance, and a teacher portal for class management. Brilliant does not publish a public developer API or partner SDK — the product is consumer- and classroom-facing, and integration with school ecosystems is limited to Google Classroom roster sync.

companies.name: Brilliant
companies.description: Brilliant is an online learning platform for interactive STEM education, covering mathematics, computer science, data, and science. Headquartered in San Francisco and used by over ten million learners worldwide, Brilliant pairs guided, problem-first lessons with adaptive practice that blends classic intelligent tutoring systems, machine-learning recommender systems, and natural-language conversations. The platform is delivered through brilliant.org and native iOS and Android apps, with a freemium model and a Brilliant Premium subscription that unlocks the full course catalog, including expanding AI-powered features such as personalized tutoring conversations and on-the-fly generation of interactive content. Brilliant operates as a direct-to-consumer subscription business with an educator program for classroom access; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program, and the `github.com/brilliant` org on GitHub is an unrelated namespace of personal projects rather than an official Brilliant presence.

companies.name: Goodfellow
companies.description: Goodfellow (Goodfellow Advanced Materials) is a global specialty-materials supplier founded in 1946 and headquartered in Cambridgeshire, United Kingdom, serving research, prototyping and specialized manufacturing markets in more than 111 countries. Its catalog spans over 70,000 stocked products drawn from 700+ different materials in many forms, including metals, alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites, compounds and glass, alongside custom fabrication and laboratory testing services. Customers include universities, government research facilities, laboratories and advanced manufacturers, served through subsidiaries in the United States, China, France and Germany. Goodfellow was acquired by Battery Ventures in 2021 to help digitize its operations and fund materials acquisitions. Goodfellow is a business-to-business e-commerce and catalog operation; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs or webhooks.

companies.name: Hyperpad
companies.description: Hyperpad (hyperPad) is a no-code, visual game development platform for iPad, often described as "HyperCard for iPad." Founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the London, Ontario company lets non-programmers build media-rich 2D games and interactive apps using a drag-and-drop, node-based behavior system with a built-in physics engine, particle effects, animation and audio tools, and a bundled asset library, then publish them to the Apple App Store as native apps while keeping 100% of royalties. Products include the paid hyperPad app, a free hyperPad Starter edition, and hyperPad Hub, a community arcade for playing games made with the platform. hyperPad is a consumer-facing creation tool and does not currently publish a public web API or developer platform.

companies.name: IXL Learning
companies.description: IXL Learning is a K-12 personalized practice platform with 17,000+ skills across Math, Language Arts, Science, Social Studies, and Spanish, plus the IXL Real-Time Diagnostic and skill recommendations. IXL is sold primarily as a SaaS subscription to families, teachers, schools, and districts. Its integration surface is school-rostering and SSO, not a public developer API: IXL supports Clever (SSO + rostering), ClassLink (SSO + OneRoster auto-rostering), OneRoster CSV/REST, LTI, Google Classroom, and SAML SSO for district deployments. There is no public REST API portal, no published OpenAPI, and no partner developer program.

companies.name: Unitree Robotics
companies.description: Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou, China-based high-performance robot manufacturer founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing. The company is a global pioneer in the commercial quadruped (robot dog) market and has expanded into bipedal humanoid robots. Its product line includes the Go1, Go2, and Go2-W quadrupeds for consumers, education, and research; the industrial-grade B1 and B2 quadrupeds for inspection, patrol, and logistics; the H1 full-size humanoid; the G1 humanoid for research and developer experimentation; the R1 humanoid; and the Z1 robotic arm. Unitree also produces in-house components including the L1/L2 LiDAR, hand-grade actuators, and dexterous hands (Dex1-1). Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

companies.name: Cajal Technologies
companies.description: Cajal Technologies (Cajal) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (W26) company scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. Its multi-agent system, Tau, collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean, deploying AI mathematicians across high-impact applied domains starting with quantum computing and finance. Tau verifies compiled binaries with mathematical certainty down to the machine level. Cajal also partners with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems through datasets, evals, and RL environments, and open-sources tooling such as Talos, a Wasm interpreter written in Lean designed for reasoning.

companies.name: Lagou
companies.description: Lagou (拉勾招聘) is a Chinese online recruitment platform operated by Beijing Lagou Network Technology Co., Ltd., focused on hiring for the internet and technology sector. It matches software engineers, product managers, designers and other digital-economy professionals with employers across major Chinese cities, publishing verified job listings alongside a browseable directory of hiring companies. Around the core job board it runs Lagou Enterprise (easy.lagou.com) for employer-side recruiting, Lagou Campus (xiaoyuan.lagou.com) for graduate hiring, and Lagou Education (kaiwu.lagou.com) for professional-skills courses. Lagou was surfaced through the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio. It publishes no public API, developer portal or API documentation — open.lagou.com carries a "Lagou Open Platform" title but serves only a stub page — so this profile captures the company's public web and security surface rather than an API surface.

companies.name: EdSights
companies.description: EdSights is a student voice and engagement platform for higher education. It pairs an AI-powered SMS chatbot with real-time analytics to collect continuous feedback from students, surface persistence and well-being risk, and flag individuals who need staff intervention. Its Student Voice Score (SVS) benchmarks student satisfaction the way NPS benchmarks customers, and institutional dashboards help retention, advising, and student-success teams act on that feedback throughout the academic journey. EdSights serves 290+ colleges and universities and connects to campus systems — Banner SIS, Slate, Salesforce, Starfish, EAB Navigate360, and Pharos — via SFTP data feeds. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this profile EdSights exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhooks; integration is data-file (SFTP) based, so most API-artifact enrichment is not applicable.

companies.name: Udacity
companies.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

companies.name: Kilsar
companies.description: Kilsar is an AI-powered maintenance training and operations platform for the aviation, defense, and industrial sectors. Its flagship product, Orion, turns static technical manuals and maintenance procedures into intelligent, guided workflows so technicians learn faster and perform complex tasks correctly. The platform provides AI-assisted search across operational and maintenance manuals, dynamic data storage and library management, custom workflow and procedure building, real-time task tracking and work-log monitoring, and predictive maintenance and troubleshooting guidance. Kilsar promises measurable outcomes including reduced downtime, faster mean-time-to-repair, and increased equipment uptime. Kilsar is a Techstars-backed company. As of this profile it publishes a marketing site and a Secureframe-hosted trust center but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: One Month
companies.description: One Month is an online coding education platform that teaches beginners practical software and web development skills through short, project-based video courses designed to be completed in about a month. Its catalog spans programming languages and frameworks such as Ruby, Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, HTML & CSS, SQL, and WordPress, alongside professional skills like project management, using a "watch, do, repeat" methodology of hands-on lessons and follow-along projects. One Month markets itself to career changers and non-programmers looking to accelerate into technical roles, and publishes a supporting blog of programming tutorials and career guidance. It is a consumer-facing learning product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: OnMyGrad
companies.description: OnMyGrad is a Hong Kong-based campus-recruitment and career-learning SaaS platform that helps employers connect with university talent across Southeast Asia through virtual job-tasting and work-experience programs. Founded in 2021 by Jesse Chow and Chun Hin Anthony So, its B2B2C "OnMyGrad Space" lets employers build branded profiles, run virtual talent pipelines, and evaluate candidates, while students access immersive career and industry learning content from leading employers. The company launched its MVP in February 2021, raised pre-seed funding from 500 Global, and is expanding into Singapore and Taiwan. It operates a public marketing site and a web application but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Pandai
companies.description: Pandai is a Malaysian education technology company founded in 2020 that operates a digital learning platform for primary and secondary school students. The app aligns to Malaysia's national curriculum (DSKP) across KSSR Years 1-6 and KSSM Forms 1-5, including SPM exam preparation, and helps learners improve their grades through interactive quizzes, tests, exams, topical practice, notes, flashcards, videos, and live tutoring. Features include personalized assessments, an AI-powered revision assistant (Ask Pbot), gamified learning with battles, leaderboards and rewards, and performance tracking via scorecards and report cards. Pandai is a consumer-facing learning app and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Prisms VR
companies.description: Prisms VR (Prisms) is an educational technology company building what it calls the world's first spatial learning platform, where students learn core math, science, and other subjects by abstracting up from immersive, first-person physical experiences delivered in virtual reality. Founded by MIT engineer-turned-educator Anurupa Ganguly, the teacher-facing platform uses kinesthetic, embodied learning to help students grasp abstract concepts and aims to develop curious, resilient thinkers. Prisms is an a16z portfolio company; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and profiled through the enrichment pipeline. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

companies.name: Skool
companies.description: Skool is an all-in-one community platform that combines discussion communities, online courses, live calls, and gamification in a single product, founded by Sam Ovens and popularized in partnership with Alex Hormozi. As of this review, Skool does NOT publish an official public or partner developer REST API. The only official programmatic surface is a Zapier integration, gated to the paid Pro plan, that exposes a small set of triggers and actions via a per-group API key used solely to link a Skool group to Zapier - it is not a general-purpose developer API. All broader "Skool API" offerings found in the wild (Apify actors, docs.skoolapi.com, reverse-engineered clients, Chrome extensions) are unofficial third-party tools built on Skool's undocumented internal endpoints and are not endorsed or supported by Skool. This catalog entry is an honest gated stub: no public API surface is modeled because none is documented.

companies.name: Zzish
companies.description: Zzish is an EdTech company (a Techstars-backed startup) building a K-12 learning product suite used by teachers and students across 180 countries. Its flagship product, Quizalize, is a classroom quiz and formative-assessment platform; the portfolio also includes Blockerzz (a 3D game engine with quiz games and coding tutorials), Marvely.ai (AI-powered, exam-aligned language tutoring), Quizalize Insights (leadership dashboards for tracking academic progress), and QUAT (a customer-analytics platform for schools and EdTech partners). Zzish reports 250k+ teachers onboarded in the last two years and 250m+ questions answered since launch. As of this enrichment pass, Zzish publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer-documentation surface.

companies.name: Avarra
companies.description: Avarra is an AI-powered sales training and enablement platform that helps revenue teams onboard, coach, and certify sales representatives at scale. The platform turns real sales conversations into AI-driven role-play simulations, delivers personalized coaching feedback, standardizes sales methodology across teams and regions, and reports certification and performance analytics. Its workflow moves through five stages: Capture, Train, Practice, Certify, and Performance Insights, with the stated goal of cutting new-hire ramp time in half. Avarra is a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company. As of this profile Avarra publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Modular Robotics
companies.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot. The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

companies.name: Nurture
companies.description: Nurture is an EdTech company that turns children's screen time into skill-building experiences through an interactive storytelling app for kids aged 5-7. Built on the thesis that AI is mastering information while human skills — critical thinking, curiosity, empathy, creativity, and resilience — still need to be nurtured, the app delivers character-driven story adventures with practice-based learning, no in-app purchases, no ads, and no endless autoplay. It is COPPA-compliant and features licensed brands such as Care Bears, Crayola, and Pocoyo. Nurture is a consumer mobile product distributed on the iOS App Store, Google Play, and Amazon Appstore, sold as a $36/year subscription with a 7-day free trial. It is a Seedcamp portfolio company. As a consumer application, Nurture publishes no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface; api.nurture.is serves only an internal app backend.

companies.name: Cleverdeck
companies.description: CleverDeck is a spaced-repetition flashcard application for iOS, built by an independent developer to help people learn and retain vocabulary and other material more efficiently. It ships hand-made premium decks covering roughly the 3,000 most common words in major foreign languages — Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, Persian, Russian and advanced English — with translations, transliterations, images, native-speaker audio, and example sentences in both English and the target language. The app uses the SM-2 spaced-repetition algorithm (as popularized by SuperMemo and Anki) with a customizable learning schedule, cross-device sync, and full offline support. It is free to create and study your own content, with unlimited access to the premium decks for $3 per month. CleverDeck is a consumer mobile product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or agent-facing surface.

companies.name: Fizz
companies.description: Fizz is a social platform built for college campuses, connecting students within their own school communities across 700+ campuses in the United States. Founded by Stanford students, Fizz gives verified students an anonymous, hyper-local feed to find their community and join the conversation, buy and sell through Fizz Marketplace, and engage under community values of being supportive, curious, honest, and brave. The platform is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and NEA. Fizz is a consumer mobile social app and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface for network discovery and monitoring.

companies.name: HumanQ
companies.description: HumanQ is an execution-capability and intelligence platform that helps organizations move critical work forward through structured, live execution sprints called QPods. Each QPod is a 60-minute facilitated session, led by trained "Catalysts," for small groups of up to six participants working through decision drag, unclear ownership, and cross-team stalls. HumanQ is offered as HumanQ Scale (an enterprise-wide program with weekly and monthly tracks, on-demand drop-ins, and deep customization) and HumanQ Teams (a manager-led tool for up to four groups, live in two weeks with no contract). Progress is tracked through the QStart, QImpact, and QSignal measurement framework, with delivery across 74 countries. HumanQ is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. It is a managed-services platform and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

companies.name: Quero Educação
companies.description: Quero Educação is a Brazilian education-technology company that operates a marketplace connecting students with higher-education institutions across Brazil. Its flagship product Quero Bolsa lets students compare colleges, courses and schools with price transparency and enroll online at discounted tuition, while a suite of institution-facing products — Nota Quero (online entrance exams), Matrícula Digital (digital enrollment), Quero Pago (tuition payments) and Quero Analytics (data intelligence) — helps partner schools fill seats and manage admissions. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company. It maintains a private GitHub organization and a public engineering blog on Medium, but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or published API documentation at this time; this profile captures its public identity, domain-security posture, and commercial/legal surfaces.

companies.name: Skillshare
companies.description: Skillshare is a New York City–based online learning community for creators, founded in 2010 by Michael Karnjanaprakorn and Malcolm Ong. The platform hosts thousands of on-demand video classes across creative disciplines — illustration, design, photography, animation, lettering, film, productivity, writing, and business — taught by working creators and industry professionals. Skillshare operates on a paid subscription model (Premium membership) that grants members unlimited access to the class catalog, project-based learning, and a discussion community where students submit class projects for feedback. The company has a teacher revenue-share program in which class creators are paid based on watch time and student enrollments, and runs Skillshare for Teams as a B2B offering for organizations to give employees access to the catalog. Skillshare does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, partner API, or SDK. The platform's programmatic surface is limited to internal web/mobile clients and an affiliate/marketing referral program; there is no documented developer portal, public webhook system, or third-party integration API for the Skillshare catalog, enrollments, watch-time, or teacher-payout data.

companies.name: Vedantu
companies.description: Vedantu is an Indian online-learning (edtech) company headquartered in Bangalore that delivers LIVE interactive classes, recorded courses, offline centres, and one-to-one tutoring for school students from Class 1 to 12 and competitive-exam aspirants, covering CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE and major State Boards plus JEE, NEET, CUET and Olympiad preparation, alongside a large free library of NCERT solutions, revision notes, sample papers and study material. Backed by Accel, Vedantu is consumer-facing and operates no public developer API today; its only published integration surface is a legacy External-Integration (EI) kit for institutes on GitHub, though it does publish an llms.txt for agents.

companies.name: Recess
companies.description: Recess (Recess Academy, recess.gg) is an online school for gifted and neurodivergent students, including learners with ADHD, dyslexia, autism spectrum, and anxiety. It combines core academics, interest-led classes, small-group coworking sessions with an AI tutor, and a daily community hour, with personalized pacing and world-class mentors. Recess is backed by Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a consumer education web application and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; the only machine-discoverable surface found is a valid RFC 9116 security.txt with a security contact.

The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. companies.name: Jade Autism

Its product family includes Jade Edu (personalized-learning software for schools and educators), the Jade App (cognitive-development games for children, with 185,000+ downloads across 179 countries), Jade Astea (eye-tracking technology that assists professionals in evaluating autism-spectrum diagnosis), and Jade Academy (professional-development courses on inclusive and diverse education). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Junto Education
companies.description: Junto is a Berlin-based leadership-development company and a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. Junto delivers cohort-based, live and interactive online training led by certified coaches who previously held senior leadership roles at leading technology companies. Its programs combine the accountability and personal interaction of offline training with the scalability of online learning, and cover first-time managers, high-performance teams, and custom leadership tracks. Junto sells directly to organizations, who nominate high-potential employees for the programs. Junto operates a marketing site at junto.eu and a customer learning application at app.junto.eu. As of this profile, Junto publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Lyra Health
companies.description: Lyra Health is a Burlingame, California enterprise mental health benefits company founded in 2015 that provides employer-sponsored behavioral health care to more than 20 million members across a network of 30,000+ providers in over 200 countries and territories. The platform combines preventive self-care resources, coaching, evidence-based therapy, medication management, family and pediatric services, and specialized acute care delivered through a benefits-administration model sold to large employers and health plans rather than directly to consumers. Lyra's product surface includes the Lyra App for members, the Lyra Empower AI-powered care platform launched in 2025, Centers of Excellence for pediatric mental health and neurodiversity, a manager coaching program, and a clinical-grade AI guide. Customers include Salesforce, Lululemon, Morgan Stanley, Genentech, Starbucks, JE Dunn, VCA, and the School District of Philadelphia, and in March 2026 the company became Workday Wellness's preferred mental health partner. Lyra acquired pediatric and family mental health provider Bend Health in July 2025. Lyra is led by CEO Jennifer Schulz, with Jenny Gonsalves as Chief Product & Technology Officer, Alethea Varra as Chief Clinical Officer, and co-founder Bob Kocher, MD on the board. The company's revenue model is per-member-per- month employer contracts plus utilization-based clinical billing; Lyra does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or self-service API, and its only public GitHub repository is an internal fork of an unrelated infrastructure module. companies.name: Atom Computing
companies.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

companies.name: Knight Frank
companies.description: Knight Frank LLP is a London-headquartered global real estate consultancy founded in 1896, structured as a partnership rather than a listed company, operating through a network of over 700 offices in more than 50 territories and best known for prime and super-prime residential agency, commercial agency and occupier services, valuation and advisory, capital markets, rural and agricultural consultancy, and the Knight Frank Research programme that publishes The Wealth Report and the Prime International Residential Index. It sits on the advisory and agency side of the property value chain rather than the data-platform side. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where there is no MLS and no cooperative listing standard — residential stock reaches consumers through the Rightmove and Zoopla duopoly by way of agency CRM software (Reapit, Alto, Street, Apex27) rather than a shared cooperative pool, so Knight Frank is a supplier into that pipe and not an operator of it. Its API posture is honest but unflattering: Knight Frank publishes no developer portal, no API programme, no developer terms, no SDK and no Postman collection, and every conventional developer entry point fails — developer., developers., docs. and apis.knightfrank.com do not resolve in DNS, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs all return 404 on knightfrank.com and knightfrank.co.uk. On the UK site /developers is a homonym trap: it redirects to a commercial services page for property developers and housebuilders, not software developers. What does exist, entirely unadvertised, is a real machine-readable contract. The corporate search service at api-v3.web.prd-knightfrank.com serves a live Swagger UI and an OpenAPI 3.0.1 document (11 GET/POST operations across CMSPage, IntelligenceLab, Office, Person, Search, ServiceLine and Telemetry) to anonymous clients, and those endpoints answer with real office and people-directory data without any credential. The property search and saved-property service at api-v2.web.prd-knightfrank.com is the opposite: it returns 401 and is protected by Azure AD B2C (tenant KnightFrankB2Cprod, custom policy B2C_1A_MYKFSIGNIN, scope MyKf.ReadWrite) through a first-party MSAL client for the consumer My Knight Frank account, which is an end-user login and not a developer credential. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the Knight Frank estate — RESO is a North American NAR/MLS construct and the United Kingdom has no MLS to certify against. Knight Frank publishes no open data either; its research ships as PDF and web narrative, and the genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector — HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey open products — not to the brokerage.

companies.name: Modal
companies.description: Modal is a serverless cloud platform for AI and data workloads. Modal lets developers write ordinary Python and run it on remote GPUs and CPUs with sub-second cold starts, instant autoscaling, and declarative container images. The platform's primitives — Functions, Sandboxes, Volumes, Images, Secrets, Dicts, Queues, Schedules, and Web Endpoints — cover inference, fine-tuning, multi-node training, batch processing, agent code execution, and HTTP/web APIs. Modal sells per-second metered compute across the full NVIDIA GPU lineup (T4 → B200) under Starter, Team, and Enterprise plans. Modal Labs raised a $355M Series C in 2026 and is used in production by Decagon, Runway, Physical Intelligence, Suno, Chai Discovery, Lovable, Quora, Reducto, and many others.

companies.name: Real Estate Institute of Australia
companies.description: The Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA), founded in 1924 and based in Canberra, is the national federation of the eight state and territory Real Estate Institutes (REINSW, REIV, REIQ, REIWA, REISA, REIT, REIACT, REINT), which between them represent roughly 85% of Australian real estate businesses and agents. REIA is a policy, research and accreditation body, not an operator of market infrastructure: it administers the REIA National Principles of Conduct that underpin state institute codes and training, awards Associate (AREI) and Fellow accreditations, runs the Australasian Auctioneering Championships (AUSTROS) jointly with REINZ and the National Awards for Excellence (NAFE), makes submissions to the Commonwealth Government, and publishes the quarterly Housing Affordability Report (HAR) and Real Estate Market Facts (REMF) series that Federal Treasury, the Reserve Bank, state treasuries and investment banks subscribe to. It sits well above the transaction rail in the Australian value chain - listings run through REA Group's realestate.com.au and Domain, settlement through PEXA, valuation through PropTrack and CoreLogic, and title through the state land registries - and REIA touches none of those pipes. Its API posture is therefore an honest absence: no developer portal, no API subdomain, no OpenAPI or OData contract, and no RESO reference anywhere on its estate, because RESO is a NAR-mandated United States construct with no Australian counterpart. What REIA sells is data, not access to it - the HAR and REMF reports are AUD 450 subscriptions and each of the 7 HAR and 15 REMF underlying datasets is a separate AUD 280 subscription, delivered as documents through a platformOS/Insites ecommerce storefront with Stripe checkout behind an email-and-password account. Policy submissions, standalone research reports and the strategic plan are freely downloadable PDFs; the quarterly numbers are not, and there is no open data.
